name: Podia
tagline: Creator platform for courses, digital products, email, and memberships

pricing.notes: Official pricing checked; public 2026 sources list Mover around $49/month monthly or $42/month annually, with transaction fees on lower tier.

tiers.name: Mover
tiers.limits: 50 products; 500 videos; 25 community spaces; 100 email subscribers; unlimited customers; 5% transaction fee.

tiers.name: Shaker
tiers.limits: 150 products; 1,000 videos; 100 community spaces; 1 assistant; 500 email subscribers; 0% transaction fee.

tiers.name: Earthquaker
tiers.limits: Unlimited products, videos, spaces and assistants; 1,000 email subscribers; 0% transaction fee.

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier; 30-day trial with no card required
pricing.hiddenCosts: Mover takes 5% of sales; email costs rise with subscriber count (the current example for 2,500 subscribers is $28/month or $22/month on annual billing); Stripe/PayPal processing is separate, and annual subscriptions generally receive no partial refund.

verdictSummary: Selling a few digital downloads or a course is buildable, but Podia bundles checkout, file delivery, courses, email, memberships, affiliates, and support.
coreLoopDIY: Build product pages, Stripe checkout, gated downloads/course lessons, customer accounts, and email receipts.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because commerce plus content delivery has lots of edge cases.

priorArt.name: Ghost
priorArt.desc: Open-source publishing and memberships; combine with Stripe/file hosting for some Podia us

alternatives.name: CourseLit
alternatives.desc: Courses, downloads, email automation and memberships in one compose file; hosting and deliverability are yours.

alternatives.name: systeme.io
alternatives.desc: One course, digital products, memberships, email and 2,000 contacts free; the second course is where the meter starts.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Ghost
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Email and memberships fit; courses, quizzes and a general digital-product store do not.

notes: Good creator monetization entry where 60% DIY value is realistic.
prompt:
Build me a small digital-products store to replace Podia, for selling a few downloads,
not running a course business. Requirements:

- Node + Express + better-sqlite3, server-rendered pages with nunjucks, deployed on my
  VPS behind my existing reverse proxy.
- Products live in products.json: slug, title, price, description, and the file to
  deliver. Delivered files sit outside the web root.
- One page per product plus a /store index. The buy button goes straight to Stripe
  Checkout (keys in .env); no cart, no coupons.
- Stripe webhook on payment: record the order in SQLite (email, product, amount,
  timestamp) and email the buyer a download link via Resend or SMTP (creds in .env).
- Download links are signed tokens that expire after 7 days or 5 uses; an expired link
  shows a resend-by-email form.
- An /admin page behind HTTP basic auth: order list and revenue per product.
- Out of scope: memberships, drip courses, email marketing, and affiliates. Do not build
  customer accounts, the receipt email is the account.
- README: Stripe webhook setup with the CLI test command, and a plain note that
  VAT/sales tax is on me, Stripe Tax exists if it matters.
